**Download Cuewand-for-Windows.zip below.** It has everything in it, Python included: there is nothing to install.

1. Extract the zip (right-click it, **Extract All**).
2. In the extracted folder, double-click **Start Cuewand.exe**. A page with a large code opens.
3. Open your deck in PowerPoint and scan the code with your phone, in either order. There is no file to choose: Cuewand finds the deck open in PowerPoint by itself, and the page says "Found your deck".

New in 2.6: Setup asks when the clock starts: when the slide show starts, with your first Next, or no clock at all (for a lesson). And a trial: zoom the slide show on the big screen from the phone (Setup, More options); try it before you rely on it.

Since 2.5: the download is built to pass **Windows Smart App Control**, which blocked 2.4's `.bat` files. The three programs (Start Cuewand, Test Cuewand, Get the internet link ready) are now `.exe` files signed by the Python Software Foundation, and Cuewand talks to PowerPoint through comtypes, so no program file in the zip is unsigned. Nothing is installed on first run any more.

When Windows asks about the firewall, tick **Public as well as Private**, then Allow. Hotel, venue and hotspot networks count as Public.

Before an important talk, open your deck and double-click **Test Cuewand.exe**: it presses through the whole deck and checks that every press lands exactly once.

Needs Windows with PowerPoint. The full manual is README.txt in the folder.
